sentences.text: Mycterosuchus was an extinct genus of teleosaurid crocodyliform that lived in England during the Middle Jurassic. The name Mycterosuchus means 'long-nosed crocodile', combining Latin and Greek roots.
This animal belongs to the family Teleosauridae and is classified within the parent group Aeolodontini.
Andrews named the genus Mycterosuchus in 1913 based on fossils from the Oxford Clay of southern England.
Mycterosuchus nasutus was synonymized with Steneosaurus leedsi in 1987 but was recovered as a distinct species in a 2018 cladistic analysis.
Mycterosuchus lived during the Callovian stage, between 165.3 and 161.5 million years ago.
Recent cladistic analysis suggests Mycterosuchus is distantly related to the type species of Steneosaurus, despite earlier synonymization.
